cards.text: Jesus just called out the Pharisees and the experts in the law at a dinner, and now the scribes and Pharisees are bitterly opposing Him, waiting to catch Him in something He says (Luke 11:53-54). Meanwhile, a crowd of many thousands has packed in so tight they're trampling one another. Friend, that's not a crowd, that's a doorbuster sale at 5 a.m.

cards.question: True or false: With thousands pressing in, Jesus starts by speaking to His disciples.

cards.text: His first words are a warning: beware of the leaven of the Pharisees. And remember, Jesus just told the Pharisees they clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they're full of greed and wickedness (Luke 11:39).

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples what the leaven of the Pharisees is. What does He call it?

cards.text: Then Jesus talks about the things people keep concealed and hidden, the back-of-the-drawer stuff. Friend, I would know.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says some things that are hidden will never be made known.

cards.text: He says what's spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what's whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops. That's every private group chat that EVER got screenshotted, friend.
Next, Jesus calls the disciples "My friends." He tells them not to be afraid of those who kill the body.

cards.question: Jesus tells His friends not to fear the people who can kill the body. What's His reason?

answers.text: After that they can do no more
They will never catch the disciples
The crowd will stand up for them

cards.question: Jesus says not to fear the people who can kill the body. Who does He say the disciples should fear instead?

answers.text: The One with authority to throw them into hell
The Pharisees who are watching Him closely
The rulers who can drag them into court

cards.text: Then Jesus points to sparrows: five of them sell for two pennies. Friend, I came out of a closing-day bin with a 25-cent sticker on me, and even I'm saying that's CHEAP.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says sparrows are so cheap that God forgets some of them.

cards.text: Then Jesus says even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. I can't keep count of my own mustache, friend, and I use it as HANDS.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples not to be afraid, because they are worth more than many ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about confessing Him before men, owning up to Him in front of people. Not a quiet little thumbs-up in the group chat, friend.

cards.question: When someone confesses Jesus before men, what does Jesus say the Son of Man will do?

answers.text: Confess him before the angels of God
Reward him in front of the crowds
Make him a ruler over Israel

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says whoever denies Him before men will be denied before the angels of God.

cards.text: Then Jesus gets serious. Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven.

cards.question: But Jesus says one kind of blasphemy will not be forgiven. Blasphemy against whom?

cards.text: Last, Jesus says the disciples will be brought before synagogues, rulers and authorities. Me? I'd be up all night practicing my speech in the bathroom mirror.

cards.question: When the disciples are brought before rulers and authorities, what does Jesus tell them not to worry about?

answers.text: How long they will be held

cards.question: Jesus says that at that time the Holy ___ will teach the disciples what they should say.

cards.text: The Holy Spirit has the words covered, so I can cancel the mirror practice. But hold that thought, friend, because this teaching is far from finished.

findings.problem: The opening card sets the previous confrontation and the gathering crowd, but it never says that Jesus' present address is to His disciples. That essential context about whom He is addressing is withheld until card 2's question.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The dinner setting and Jesus' rebukes of the Pharisees and experts in the law come earlier in Luke 11. The card's only outside-passage reference, Luke 11:53-54, supports the bitter opposition and attempt to catch Him, not those earlier facts.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This asks for the unseen wording of verse 12 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out. The earlier cards establish that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is unforgivable and that the disciples need not prepare a defense, but they give no basis for deciding that the Spirit, rather than the Scriptures or angels, will teach them what to say.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
